title: The Battle of Vicksburg
summary: Follow Grant's 1863 march to Vicksburg along the Mississippi River, and see why taking the city split the Confederacy in two.
subject: History

compellingQuestion.en: Why did the Union need Vicksburg, and how did Grant take it?
compellingQuestion.es: ¿Por qué necesitaba la Unión a Vicksburg y cómo la tomó Grant?

questions.task: Open The Battle of Vicksburg bookmark. Vicksburg is the yellow pin. Look at where it sits on the Mississippi River and, zoomed in (the railroads only show at closer scales), where the railroad leads east. Why would both sides want the city?

student.en: Open The Battle of Vicksburg bookmark. Vicksburg is the yellow pin on the Mississippi River. Zoom in until the railroads appear: where does the railroad from Vicksburg lead? Why would both sides want the city?
student.es: Abre el marcador The Battle of Vicksburg. Vicksburg es el alfiler amarillo junto al río Misisipi. Acércate hasta que aparezcan los ferrocarriles: ¿a dónde lleva el ferrocarril que sale de Vicksburg? ¿Por qué querrían la ciudad ambos lados?

answer.text: Vicksburg stands on high bluffs over a bend in the Mississippi, so its guns controlled traffic on the river. A railroad ran east to Jackson, linking the river to the rest of the Confederacy. Whoever held Vicksburg controlled the river between the Confederacy's eastern and western states.

questions.task: Find the key places and put them in order along Grant's route: Milliken's Bend, New Carthage, Hard Times, Bruinsburg Bend, then Edwards. Measure the distance from Milliken's Bend to Bruinsburg Bend.

student.en: Find the dark pins for Milliken's Bend, New Carthage, Hard Times, Bruinsburg Bend and Edwards. Which side of the river is each on? Why did Grant march south before crossing the river?
student.es: Busca los alfileres oscuros de Milliken's Bend, New Carthage, Hard Times, Bruinsburg Bend y Edwards. ¿De qué lado del río está cada lugar? ¿Por qué marchó Grant hacia el sur antes de cruzar el río?

fill.en: Measure the distance from Milliken's Bend to Bruinsburg Bend: ________ miles
fill.es: Mide la distancia de Milliken's Bend a Bruinsburg Bend: ________ millas

answer.text: Milliken's Bend, New Carthage and Hard Times are on the Louisiana (west) side; Bruinsburg Bend and Edwards are in Mississippi. Vicksburg's guns and the swamps north of the city made a direct attack too hard, so Grant marched south down the Louisiana side and crossed the river at Bruinsburg on April 30, 1863, then turned northeast. Milliken's Bend to Bruinsburg Bend is about 33 miles (53 km) in a straight line.

questions.task: Turn on Civil War Battlefields and click the diamonds between Bruinsburg and Vicksburg. Put the battles in order by date.

student.en: In Map layers, turn on Civil War Battlefields. Click the diamonds between Bruinsburg and Vicksburg and list the battles in order by date.
student.es: En las capas del mapa (Map layers), activa Civil War Battlefields (campos de batalla de la Guerra Civil). Haz clic en los rombos entre Bruinsburg y Vicksburg y ordena las batallas por fecha.

table.caption: Battles of Grant's Vicksburg campaign, from the pop-ups

answer.text: Grand Gulf (April 29, 1863) was the Union navy's failed attack just before the crossing at Bruinsburg.

questions.task: Zoom out to see the whole Mississippi River. After Vicksburg surrendered on July 4, 1863, which Confederate states were cut off from the rest?

student.en: Zoom out to see the whole Mississippi River. Vicksburg surrendered on July 4, 1863. Which Confederate states were cut off west of the river?
student.es: Aléjate para ver todo el río Misisipi. Vicksburg se rindió el 4 de julio de 1863. ¿Qué estados confederados quedaron aislados al oeste del río?

answer.text: Texas, Arkansas and most of Louisiana. After Port Hudson, Louisiana, surrendered on July 9, 1863, the Union controlled the whole river.

final.teacher: Students answer with evidence from at least two places on the map. Some ways to do it: a paragraph, Grant's route sketched on the map, or bookmarks saved for a short talk.

student.en: Answer the big question using evidence from at least two places on the map. You can write a paragraph, sketch on the map, or both.
student.es: Responde la pregunta central con evidencia de al menos dos lugares del mapa. Puedes escribir un párrafo, dibujar en el mapa o hacer ambas cosas.

beforeYouStart.en: In 1862, Union forces captured New Orleans and Memphis, two cities on the Mississippi River. Between the two, the Confederates still held part of the river, including the city of Vicksburg, Mississippi. In spring 1863, Union General Ulysses S. Grant set out to capture it.
beforeYouStart.es: En 1862, las fuerzas de la Unión tomaron Nueva Orleans y Memphis, dos ciudades a orillas del río Misisipi. Entre ambas, los confederados todavía controlaban parte del río, incluida la ciudad de Vicksburg, en Misisipi. En la primavera de 1863, el general de la Unión Ulysses S. Grant se propuso tomarla.

readingTheMap.en: The yellow pin is Vicksburg. Dark pins mark places on Grant's route, each with its name. Railroads are thin dark lines with short cross marks, like a track; they appear when you zoom in, and they include lines built after the war. Civil War Battlefields is off when the map opens: turn it on in Map layers. Its diamonds mark battles: blue for a Union victory, gray for a Confederate victory, yellow if neither side won.
readingTheMap.es: El alfiler amarillo es Vicksburg. Los alfileres oscuros marcan lugares de la ruta de Grant, cada uno con su nombre. Los ferrocarriles son líneas oscuras finas con pequeñas marcas transversales, como una vía; aparecen al acercarte e incluyen líneas construidas después de la guerra. La capa Civil War Battlefields está desactivada al abrir el mapa: actívala en las capas del mapa (Map layers). Sus rombos marcan las batallas: azul si ganó la Unión, gris si ganó la Confederación y amarillo si ningún bando ganó.

reflection.en: What did the map show you about the Vicksburg campaign that you might not have noticed from reading alone?
reflection.es: ¿Qué te mostró el mapa sobre la campaña de Vicksburg que quizá no habrías notado solo con la lectura?

teacherNotes.beforeClass: Civil War Battlefields is off when the map opens. The railroad layer shows lines built up to 1911, so some did not exist in 1863. The key places have labels but no pop-ups.

misconceptions.claim: Grant attacked Vicksburg straight across the river.
misconceptions.response: The key places show he marched south on the Louisiana side and crossed at Bruinsburg, well south of the city.

misconceptions.claim: Vicksburg fell in a single battle.
misconceptions.response: Its pop-up gives May 18 to July 4, 1863: a siege of about six weeks.

misconceptions.claim: Gettysburg was the only turning point of July 1863.
misconceptions.response: Vicksburg surrendered on July 4, 1863, the day after Gettysburg ended, and gave the Union the Mississippi.

standards.text: Explain the causes, course, and consequence of the Civil War (sectionalism, slavery, states' rights, balance of power in the Senate)
Analyze the effects of physical and human geographic factors such as weather, landforms, waterways, transportation, and communication on major historical events in the United States
Use maps, satellite images, photographs, and other representations to explain relationships between the locations of places and regions, and changes in their environmental characteristics
Explain multiple causes and effects of events and developments in the past

keyFacts: Battles of the campaign, from the Civil War Battlefields pop-ups: Grand Gulf, April 29, 1863; Port Gibson, May 1; Raymond, May 12; Jackson, May 14; Champion Hill, May 16; Big Black River Bridge, May 17; Vicksburg, May 18 to July 4, 1863.
Grant crossed the Mississippi at Bruinsburg on April 30, 1863.
Vicksburg surrendered on July 4, 1863; Port Hudson, Louisiana, on July 9, 1863.
Milliken's Bend to Bruinsburg Bend: about 33 miles (53 km) in a straight line.
